en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is a highly active stratovolcano famous for its near-perfect symmetrical cone shape.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, has huge eyes that are actually larger than its brain.
The Cagayan River in Northern Luzon is the longest and largest river in the Philippines by volume.
Taal Lake in Batangas is a freshwater lake located entirely inside the large caldera of Taal Volcano.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Verde Island Passage between Batangas and Mindoro is known as the center of marine shorefish biodiversity.
The Philippines is the top global producer of abaca, a banana plant whose fibers make strong ropes.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river flowing directly into the sea.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon that brings dry weather to the Philippines from November to February.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected UNESCO World Heritage site for coral reefs.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are ancient man-made terraces carved into the mountains over two thousand years ago.
